x: Green and Elson, automatically in the lead, walked in "harness" for 1½ laps, when the former piled on a pace which Elson could not maintain, and wisely resigned premier honours to his club-mate. Amer (S.W.C.) was third. Green's time for the 3 miles was 23m. 7s.

Over the last mile, Amer, a Surrey stalwart, made a gallant attempt to catch and pass Joe King. This would have given our Surrey friends victory by one point; but Joe, with an equally fine effort, held his position and in the final stages of the race was even getting away from his rival.
On only one occasion has this championship been won with a lower score, viz., in 1919, when the Surrey Walking Club, represented by Blackmore, Amer, Chilton and Archibald, scored 22 points only.

Here we had Don Brown, fresh from his win in the Surrey County Championship, and Percy Wright, opposed by Hancock and Amer, of S.W.C. Our chance had gone, but our rivalry still continued, and there was still second place in the competition to be consolidated.
